archetypes.name: merge-review-integration
archetypes.rationale: The REVIEW_REQUIRED detection fires inside the not-pr_checks_all_pass branch, which can trigger premature admin-merge attempts when CI is independently pending or failing alongside a review requirement, risking misclassified stalls and side-effects from a merge attempt that was never appropriate.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the merge.py REVIEW_REQUIRED detection path: `pr_review_decision` is called every time `pr_checks_all_pass()` returns False, including when CI checks are merely pending or failing for reasons unrelated to review. Verify whether `_attempt_merge` with admin can actually succeed when CI is also blocking (admin bypass scope on GitHub branch protections varies by ruleset), and whether a failed admin merge in that scenario surfaces a misleading 'review-required' error that obscures the real CI failure. Check that `MERGE_RESULT_REVIEW_REQUIRED` is excluded from `POST_MERGE_MERGE_RESULTS` so the ship loop does not advance post-merge state on this path, and that no iteration counter increment occurs before the early terminal return in ship.py. Confirm `_write_terminal_state` receives correct iteration, rebase_count, and fix_attempts arguments consistent with what other terminal paths pass at the same site. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
